thread.title: Ams AG Decimated On Further Apple Shortfalls - AMS AG ADR (OTCMKTS:AMSSY)

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: Ams AG Decimated On Further Apple Shortfalls - AMS AG ADR (OTCMKTS:AMSSY)
text:
It’s been a brutal stretch for companies exposed to 3D sensing, with ams AG ( OTCPK:AMSSY ) (AMS.S) and IQE ( OTC:IQEPY ) having a particularly rough year. Recent weakness tied to Apple ( AAPL ) has hit the sector hard (including Lumentum ( LITE ) ), and weak volumes, underutilized capacity, and price pressure have all combined to savage ams’s near-term earning prospects and share price.
Sell-side analysts have slashed their price targets for ams by two thirds over the past four months, with one analyst going from a target of CHF 190 to CHF 23.60, and it remains to be seen just how quickly Android adoption of 3D sensing will develop and whether OEMs will favor the structured light technology where ams is strongest. Although the shares do look undervalued even after a sharp revision to expectations, this isn’t a hill I’m particularly eager to die on and investors need to weigh the potential of 3D sensing adoption against the risk that the adoption curve will be long enough that ams’s advantages will be whittled away by lower-priced Asian suppliers.
The Poison Apple ams generates around half of its revenue from Apple, and the company’s model has been predicated on healthy sales of Apple’s newest iPhones. Once again, though, that seems to not be happening, as there has been a mid-teens reduction in iPhone build assumptions due to weak demand for the new lineup (particularly the XR, as it relates to ams), and a slew of downward earnings guidance revisions from Apple suppliers like Lumentum, IQE, Qorvo ( QRVO ).
There was no place for ams to hide, and the company sharply revised its guidance in mid-November, lowering fourth quarter revenue expectations by 15% at the midpoint. The shortfall is also hitting margins, with management revising its adjusted operating margin target down to the low-to-mid teens from 16%-20% post-Q3 and the high 20%’s before third quarter earnings were reported.
At this point, not much is going right for ams vis a vis the Apple relationship. The business model has been highly dependent upon Apple 3D sensing adoption and sell-through of higher-end phones, and that’s not happening. And while the shortfalls don’t seem to be due to any performance issues with the 3D sensing, and the guidance revisions were in line with Lumentum and IQE, that really doesn’t soothe the wound all that much.
The company invested in meaningful capacity expansion to serve Apple, and that capacity is now under-utilized. Worse still, Apple is squeezing hard on pricing (as it often does), with Apple electing to use an older technology for the 2018 line-up and pushing for a double-digit cut on ASPs relative to 2017 levels. Looking ahead, Apple will likely have the option to continue turning the screws on pricing, as it is the only phone OEM offering meaningful volume for 3D sensing components at this point – ams has won business with other OEMs like Xiaomi and Huawei , but those companies are only putting 3D sensing on a small number of relatively low-volume high-end models.
Still Waiting For The 3D World Although 3D sensing may eventually become a standard feature on smartphones, that is certainly not the case today. Between the slow adoption of Android OEMs and the weak sell-through of new Apple models, ams management withdrew its guidance beyond the next quarter, and in place of a prior management target of $2.7 billion in revenue for 2019, the sell-side average estimate is now about $1.9 billion.
It hasn’t been all bad news for ams, though. The company now has two companies using its VCSELs for time-of-flight 3D sensing and will likely try to unseat Lumentum to supply the VCSEL for Apple (whether they succeed is another story). The company also announced a spectral sensor win for 2019 (most likely Xiaomi) that should contribute meaningful revenue. Management has also seen solid interest in its light sensing, active noise cancellation, and spectral sensing in other consumer applications.
What comes next, though, is clearly a big unknown. I can’t see how Huawei or Xiaomi will replace the revenue investors hoped ams would garner through Apple, and excess capacity is going to weigh a while longer. Deemphasizing the environmental sensing business in favor of optical sensing makes sense given that environmental sensing is a fragmented market with low ASPs, but while that was a good decision, I can’t say the same about management’s comments about possibly pursuing a Hong Kong listing in mid-2019.
It’s also unclear that ams will win the strong position in 3D sensing that once seemed attainable. There are other approaches beyond wafer-level optics, and a move away from wafer-level optics would seriously damage ams’s prospects. While I believe the structured light platform that ams offers has a lot of advantages, customers may choose other options, and the slower adoption curve creates more time for would-be competitors (particularly lower-cost Asian suppliers) to get into the market.
The Opportunity With the sharp disappointment in Apple volumes (and pricing) combined with the slower pace of adoption of 3D sensing among Android OEMs, the future for ams is a great deal murkier now. While I still believe mid-teens long-term revenue growth is possible (closer to 13% rather than 16% now), my mid-term growth rate estimate drops by more than 5% and I’m now using a higher discount rate to reflect the greater modeling/market uncertainties. Although a low 20%’s FCF margin could still be possible, I’m lowering my margin expectations until the company can demonstrate a stronger path toward strong and sustainable FCF generation.
The Bottom Line Although ams shares are trading below my sharply lower new fair value range ($17 to $23 for the ADRs), it’s hard to have much confidence in the modeling assumptions at this point given how dependent the company is on Apple. While it is true that there’s money to be made when everybody else gives up hope, the future of the 3D sensing market (adoption rate, volumes, ASPs) seems much more uncertain now. I’m not sure whether this is now the point of “peak disappointment” for 3D sensing, but investors considering these shares now will certainly need patience to see the story work out.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
